original_question: Let g(n) denote the least number of edges of a graph that contains a cycle of length k for every integer 1 ≤ k ≤ n. Is it true that g(n) = n + log2 n + O(1) as n → ∞?
target_in_paper: Section 1 ("Erdős Problem 1"), Conjecture 1.16 (Jia [25]), following the unnumbered definition of g(n) and Corollary 1.15.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the parameter g(n), the requirement that the graph contain a cycle of each length k up to n, the asymptotic claim n + log_2 n + O(1), and the limit regime n→∞. This matches the official open problem stated as Conjecture 1.16.
missing_details: The paper presents this specifically as Jia’s conjecture in Section 1, immediately after Theorem 1.14 and Corollary 1.15.
The minimization defining g(n) is over all graphs; the paper does not fix the number of vertices of the graph.
The logarithm is base 2 in the surrounding results and conjecture, so the notation should be written as log_2.

The nearby context matters: Theorem 1.13 and Theorem 1.14 yield Corollary 1.15, namely g(n)=n+log_2 n+O(log_2 log_2 n) for sufficiently large n; the conjecture asks whether this error term can be improved to O(1).

The graph convention is left implicit in the paper, even though the statement asks for cycles of lengths 1 and 2; a paper-faithful rewrite should preserve the paper’s wording and should not silently replace 'graph' by 'simple graph'.

No algebraic ambient structure, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or ring/field data are relevant here; the only hidden assumptions are asymptotic notation, base-2 logarithm, and the implicit graph convention.
refined_question: Is Jia’s conjecture true that, if g(n) is the minimum, over all graphs, of the number of edges in a graph containing a cycle of every length k=1,2,\dots,n, then g(n)=n+\log_2 n+O(1) as n\to\infty?
justification: The draft points directly to the unnumbered definition of g(n) in Section 1 and to Conjecture 1.16. The surrounding statements Theorem 1.13, Theorem 1.14, and Corollary 1.15 provide the exact asymptotic context: for sufficiently large n, Jia proved bounds implying g(n)=n+log_2 n+O(log_2 log_2 n). Therefore the paper’s precise open question is whether that error term can be sharpened from O(log_2 log_2 n) to O(1), and your draft already captures that core claim almost verbatim.
